classification.difficultyReason: Choose plausible measurements and assumptions, combine them into practical estimates, explain the method and round to one significant figure.

content.prompt: Estimate each of the following, correct to 1 significant figure, using appropriate units. In each case explain how you obtained your answer.

children.label: a
children.prompt: The thickness of a sheet of paper

answer.short: Sample answer: $1\times10^{-1}\text{ mm}$, using a stack of 100 sheets about 10 mm thick.
answer.worked:
Measure a stack of 100 sheets as approximately 10 mm thick, excluding covers.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Thickness per sheet}&\approx\frac{10}{100}\text{ mm}\\\text{Thickness per sheet}&\approx1\times10^{-1}\text{ mm}\quad\text{(1 significant figure).}\end{align*}$$

answer.short: Sample answer: $2\times10^2\text{ m}^3$, assuming a classroom approximately 8 m long, 7 m wide and 3 m high.
answer.worked:
Approximate the classroom by a rectangular prism measuring 8 m by 7 m by 3 m.
$$\begin{align*}V&\approx8\times7\times3\text{ m}^3\\V&\approx168\text{ m}^3\\V&\approx2\times10^2\text{ m}^3\quad\text{(1 significant figure).}\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: The height of a six-storey building

answer.short: Sample answer: $2\times10^1\text{ m}$, allowing approximately 3 m per storey.
answer.worked:
Allow approximately 3 m for each storey, including its floor structure.
$$\begin{align*}h&\approx6\times3\text{ m}\\h&\approx18\text{ m}\\h&\approx2\times10^1\text{ m}\quad\text{(1 significant figure).}\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: The area required for a car park for 500 cars

answer.short: Sample answer: $1\times10^4\text{ m}^2$, allowing approximately 25 m² per car for parking and access lanes.
answer.worked:
Assume each parking bay is approximately 5 m by 2.5 m. Double the bay area to allow for access lanes.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Area per car}&\approx2\times5\times2.5\text{ m}^2\\\text{Area per car}&\approx25\text{ m}^2\\\text{Total area}&\approx500\times25\text{ m}^2\\\text{Total area}&\approx1\times10^4\text{ m}^2\quad\text{(1 significant figure).}\end{align*}$$

children.label: e
children.prompt: The total printed area of a 600-page novel

answer.short: Sample answer: $1\times10^1\text{ m}^2$, assuming a printed region of approximately 10 cm by 18 cm on each of 600 pages.
answer.worked:
Assume the printed region on each page measures approximately 0.10 m by 0.18 m. Each numbered page is one printed side, so use 600 printed regions.
$$\begin{align*}A&\approx600\times0.10\times0.18\text{ m}^2\\A&\approx10.8\text{ m}^2\\A&\approx1\times10^1\text{ m}^2\quad\text{(1 significant figure).}\end{align*}$$

children.label: f
children.prompt: The volume of a warehouse that can store 300 000 pairs of shoes (still in their boxes)

answer.short: Sample answer: $8\times10^3\text{ m}^3$, assuming boxes measuring approximately 0.35 m by 0.20 m by 0.15 m and allowing 2.5 times their combined volume for storage and access.
answer.worked:
Assume one pair per box, with each box approximately 0.35 m by 0.20 m by 0.15 m. Allow a factor of 2.5 for aisles, shelving and unused space.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Box volume}&\approx0.35\times0.20\times0.15\text{ m}^3\\\text{Box volume}&\approx0.0105\text{ m}^3\\\text{Warehouse volume}&\approx300\,000\times0.0105\times2.5\text{ m}^3\\\text{Warehouse volume}&\approx7875\text{ m}^3\\\text{Warehouse volume}&\approx8\times10^3\text{ m}^3\quad\text{(1 significant figure).}\end{align*}$$

inlines.text: The length of a queue if every student in your school is standing in it
Discuss your answers with others in your class and with your teacher.

answer.short: Sample answer: $6\times10^2\text{ m}$, assuming 1000 students and an allowance of 0.6 m along the queue per student.
answer.worked:
For a school of approximately 1000 students, allow 0.6 m along the queue for each student, including the gap ahead.
$$\begin{align*}L&\approx1000\times0.6\text{ m}\\L&\approx6\times10^2\text{ m}\quad\text{(1 significant figure).}\end{align*}$$
